$comment: Backup scope for the durable entities added by Plan B (Task 043C).
This file is the single source of truth. docs/backup.md renders it,
tools/backup-coverage.test.mjs fails if the three drift apart.
Why a file and not a table in prose: the drill has to know which tables to
count, the job has to know which tables to dump, and a responder has to know
what to restore first. Three hand-maintained lists drift; one does not.

postgres.note: WAL archiving is the RPO. This CronJob is the SELECTABLE artefact: it is what a responder restores from when a PITR is not the answer, and what the drill proves is restorable without a provider CLI.

media.note: Not in PostgreSQL. A database restore does not bring back a media file; the drill verifies both halves against each other for this reason.

mechanism.restoreAccess: service-role only; every drill action audited

newEntityGroups.title: Tenant users
newEntityGroups.why: The identity row every other subject is scoped to. A restore without it is a restore nobody can log in to.

newEntityGroups.title: User preferences
newEntityGroups.why: Key/value per (tenant, user). Cheap to lose functionally, expensive to lose as a product promise, and `settings_version` on the project row makes a partial restore visible.

newEntityGroups.title: Notifications
newEntityGroups.why: Expires by `expires_at`; rows older than the retention window are not user-visible even when restored. A restore is correct without them, and must not be reported as a partial success because they are absent.

newEntityGroups.title: Activity events
newEntityGroups.why: Append-only feed rendered by `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/activity`. History, not state: recoverable, and the absence of a window is a gap to record rather than a reason to refuse the restore.

newEntityGroups.title: Project memberships
newEntityGroups.why: Authorization state. Restoring rows without memberships turns every project into a 403 for every non-owner, which reads as a broken release and is not one.

newEntityGroups.title: Voice preview jobs
newEntityGroups.why: Rows in a terminal state are history; rows in `Running` are a claim on a worker that no longer exists. The drill restores them as-is and the forward-fix is a reaper, not a rollback.

newEntityGroups.title: Extended project metadata
newEntityGroups.why: `dubbing_projects` predates Plan B; the nine columns are new. A base backup taken before the expand migration restores the table WITHOUT them, and the application then reads a null `name` and an unset `owner_user_id` - which is why the drill asserts the columns and not just the row count.

parents.$comment: Not new, and not a Plan B deliverable. Listed because none of the seven groups has a foreign key to its parent, so a partial restore is silent - see referentialChecks in the drill.

notInPostgres.title: Media assets, previews, exports, output
notInPostgres.why: The single most important fact in this file. A database restore does not bring back a media file and a media restore does not bring back the row describing it.

durableEntitiesNotYetBackedUp.$comment: Empty by design. An entry here is a release blocker, not a note.
